evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: `manager_restarted` only checks that the manager PID and invocation ID are nonempty and changed. It never requires the guest boot ID to be nonempty and unchanged across the manager before/after snapshots. A guest reboot also changes the manager PID and invocation ID, so this condition can pass because of a reboot rather than a manager restart within the same boot, confounding the separate `boot_id_changed` reboot check. Requiring equal nonempty boot IDs on both sides is a routine correctness fix.
